dominant_strengths: Native macOS feel — refined app icon with depth, clean SF-style typography, and a calm grayscale-plus-blue palette that feels Apple-coherent.
Strong minimalism: generous whitespace, single hero focus, and a confident hierarchy from icon → wordmark → tagline → CTA.
Polished icon craft with subtle shadow and chamfer creates a tactile centerpiece that anchors the otherwise sparse landing.
dominant_weaknesses: Composition floats — content sits high-center with a strange diagonal seam at bottom, leaving the lower half empty and unresolved.
Single weak CTA: 'Watch Introduction Video' is the only action, with no Download/Buy/Pricing path on a product landing page.
Low distinctiveness — it reads as a generic Apple-style splash; nothing communicates Things' unique task philosophy or product UI.
fix_priorities: Add a primary purchase/download CTA and platform availability beneath the tagline to convert visitors.
Replace the empty lower half with a product screenshot or feature preview to show the actual app, not just the icon.
Resolve the diagonal bottom edge — either commit to a section transition or remove it; right now it looks like a render artifact.
Tighten vertical rhythm: the icon-to-wordmark gap and tagline-to-CTA spacing feel inconsistent.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leads via the polished icon, but behavioral utility is thin (no real CTA) and reflective payoff is muted because the page never reveals the product itself.
rationale.intent_fit: It captures the Things brand surface convincingly but underperforms as a Mac-app marketing page by hiding the product UI and omitting purchase actions.
